questions.question: A persistent class MyApp.Order is defined in IRIS. What is the corresponding SQL table name?
questions.explanation: IRIS maps class package dots to underscores in SQL. MyApp.Order → SQL table MyApp_Order.

questions.question: Which Dynamic SQL method prepares and executes a query in a single step without calling %Prepare first?
questions.explanation: ##class(%SQL.Statement).%ExecDirect(, sqlString, args...) prepares and executes in one call. Useful for one-off queries where you don't need to reuse the prepared statement.

questions.question: What does the following Dynamic SQL code print if a person with Age > 25 exists?

options.text: Nothing — %Get requires a column index, not a name
The name of each person with Age > 25, one per line
Error — ? is not valid in Dynamic SQL; use :var instead

questions.explanation: ? is the correct placeholder for Dynamic SQL in IRIS. rs.%Get("ColumnName") retrieves by name. The loop prints each matching person's name.

questions.question: After running &sql(SELECT Name INTO :name FROM MyApp.Person WHERE %ID = :id), which variable tells you whether the query succeeded?
questions.explanation: After every &sql(...) statement, IRIS automatically sets the SQLCODE variable (no % prefix) in the current scope. %msg holds the error text when SQLCODE < 0.

questions.question: What does SQLCODE = 100 mean after an Embedded SQL statement?

options.text: The query executed successfully with data returned
No data was found (end of cursor or no matching row)

questions.explanation: SQLCODE = 100 is the no data code — the query ran successfully but found no matching rows, or the cursor has reached the end of the result set.

questions.question: Which of the following are correct ways to avoid SQL injection in IRIS Dynamic SQL? (select all that apply)

options.text: Use ? placeholders and pass values to %Execute()
Concatenate user input directly into the query string after calling $ZCONVERT
Use Embedded SQL with :variable host variables

questions.explanation: Using ? with %Execute, using %Prepare with parameters, and using Embedded SQL :variables all prevent SQL injection. Directly concatenating user input — even after $ZCONVERT — is never safe.

questions.question: What is the correct order of operations when using a cursor in Embedded SQL?

options.text: DECLARE → OPEN → FETCH (loop until SQLCODE ≠ 0) → CLOSE

questions.explanation: The correct cursor lifecycle is: DECLARE (define the cursor) → OPEN (execute) → FETCH in a loop until SQLCODE ≠ 0 → CLOSE.

questions.question: A Class Query named FindByAge is defined in MyApp.Person. How do you call it from ObjectScript?
questions.explanation: IRIS auto-generates a method named <QueryName>Func() for each Class Query. For FindByAge, the generated method is FindByAgeFunc(pMinAge).

questions.question: What does the following code print if no person with ID 99 exists?
questions.explanation: When no row matches, Embedded SQL sets SQLCODE = 100 (no data found). The ELSEIF SQLCODE = 100 branch fires and prints Not found.

questions.question: After a successful INSERT using Dynamic SQL, which result set property gives you the ID of the newly inserted row?
questions.explanation: After a Dynamic SQL INSERT, rs.%ROWID contains the %ID of the newly inserted row. rs.%ROWCOUNT holds the number of affected rows.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Embedded SQL compared to Dynamic SQL? (select all that apply)

options.text: Embedded SQL is checked for syntax errors at compile time
Embedded SQL uses :variable host variables; Dynamic SQL uses ? placeholders
Embedded SQL is generally faster because it is pre-compiled
Embedded SQL can accept a fully dynamic table name at runtime
Both Embedded SQL and Dynamic SQL set the SQLCODE variable after execution

questions.explanation: A: Embedded SQL syntax is validated at compile time. B: Correct — :var vs ?. C: Embedded SQL is pre-compiled and faster for fixed queries. D: Wrong — Embedded SQL cannot use dynamic table names at runtime. E: False — the local SQLCODE variable is only set automatically by Embedded SQL; in Dynamic SQL you check rs.%SQLCODE.

questions.question: Which SQLCODE value indicates a unique constraint violation (duplicate key)?
questions.explanation: SQLCODE = -119 indicates a unique constraint violation (duplicate key). SQLCODE = 100 is no data. Any negative SQLCODE is an error; -119 specifically means uniqueness was violated.
